note.after_visit_summary: Today we looked at your warts and the rough bumps on your arms. You have common warts on your fingers and knee that we treated with freezing. The bumps on your arms are keratosis pilaris, a harmless condition that often improves with age. The freezing may cause redness, blistering, or darkening of the warts over the next few days — this is normal. If sore, you can take children's acetaminophen as directed on the package. Once healed (about a week), restart the salicylic acid treatment: soak, gently file the dead skin with your own emery board, apply the acid, and cover with duct tape to help it work and prevent spreading. For your arms, use a gentle soap, avoid scrubbing, and apply urea 10% cream once a day after bathing to smooth the skin. Try not to pick or bite the warts, as this can spread them. You can go to school and play sports as normal. We’ll see you back in 3-4 weeks for another freezing session. Call us if a wart becomes very red, swollen, or oozing pus.
